L22: # Employer-specific work permits
L23: 
L24: There are 2 types of work permits: employer-specific work permits and 【4†open work permits】.
L25: 
L26: To be eligible for an employer-specific work permit, you need to meet certain requirements. Also, your Canadian employer needs to take steps before you can apply.
L27: ## On this page

L34: ## What is an employer-specific work permit
L35: 
L36: An employer-specific work permit lets you work in Canada under the conditions of the permit until the expiry date. The details are listed on your permit under the following sections:
L37: 
L38:   * Additional Information – includes the employer, location and occupation
L39:   * Conditions – consists of a numbered list of requirements you need to meet
L40:   * Remarks – may contain additional clarifications or conditions that you may need to meet
L41: See an 【10†example of a work permit】.
L42: ### Sample of the current version of an IMM 1442 work permit
L43: 
L44: 【11†Image: Sample of the current version of an IMM 1442 work permit】
L45: 
L46: You must comply with all the information listed on your work permit.
L47: 
L48: ### Popular employer-specific work permits
L49: 
L50:   * 【12†International Experience Canada (Young Professionals category)】
L51:   * 【13†Global Skills Strategy】
L52:   * 【14†agricultural workers】
L53:   * 【15†all employer-specific work permits with special instructions】
L54: ## What you need to apply
L55: 
L56: To apply for an employer-specific work permit, you need
L57: 
L58:   * to have a job offer from an employer who’s not on the list of 【16†non-compliant employers】
L59:   * to meet the general requirements for all work permit applicants
L60: 
L61: Some people 【17†don’t need a work permit】 to work in Canada. If you need a work permit and don’t yet have one, you can’t
L62: 
L63:   * legally work in Canada or
L64:   * write on a job application that you’re legally allowed to work in Canada
L65: ### Don’t have a job offer?
L66: 
L67: 【18†Search jobs for temporary foreign workers on the Job Bank†www.jobbank.gc.ca】.
L68: ## Ask your employer about a labour market impact assessment
L69: 
L70: A labour market impact assessment (LMIA) is a document that proves there’s a need to hire a foreign worker to fill the job. Most jobs need an LMIA.
L71: 
L72: Before you apply for a work permit, your employer needs to
L73: 
L74:   * find out if they need an LMIA for your job or if it’s LMIA-exempt
L75:   * apply for an LMIA (if needed)
L76:   * give you documents, like an LMIA letter and Annex A from their positive LMIA, which you’ll need to include in your application
L77: ### Are you an employer?
L78: 
L79: 【19†Find out if you need an LMIA to hire a temporary foreign worker】.
L80:

L82:

L84: 
L85:   * if an employer-specific work permit is right for you
L86:   * if you need to follow special instructions to apply

L36: # How to hire a worker
L37: ## On this page
L38: 
L39:   * 【11†Submit an offer of employment】

L43: ## Submit an offer of employment
L44: 
L45: Work permit extension for workers in Quebec
L46: 
L47: Starting March 13, 2026, your worker may be eligible for a labour market impact assessment (LMIA) exemption.
L48: 
L49: 【15†Find out more about this exemption】.
L50: 
L51: In most cases, to hire a temporary worker through the International Mobility Program, you must
L52: 
L53:   * pay the employer compliance fee of $230 and
L54:   * create and submit an offer of employment form through the 【4†Employer Portal】.
L55: Your offer of employment must include information about
L56: 
L57:   * your business
L58:   * the foreign worker you’d like to hire
L59:   * the job details
L60:   * wage and benefits
L61: ### Special requirements for hiring certain types of foreign workers
L62: 
L63: Depending on the type of worker you plan to hire, there may be special requirements you need to meet.
L64: 
L65: Hiring French-speaking or bilingual worker outside Quebec
L66: 
L67: You can hire a French-speaking or bilingual worker outside Quebec without an LMIA if the worker
L68: 
L69:   * can communicate with a moderate proficiency for speaking and listening in French
L70:   * will live and work outside the province of Quebec
L71: 【16†Learn more about hiring a French-speaking or bilingual worker outside Quebec】.
L72: 
L73: Hiring an overnight camp counsellor
L74: 
L75: You can hire an overnight camp counsellor through the International Mobility Program. If your worker fits the description, you don’t need to get a labour market impact assessment (LMIA). You may also be exempt from paying the employer compliance fee, depending on the worker’s situation.
L76: 
L77: 【17†Learn more about hiring an overnight camp counsellor】.
L78: Hiring a worker under the Innovation Stream
L79: 
L80: You can hire a foreign worker without an LMIA if you’re an employer participating in the 【18†Global Hypergrowth Project (GHP)†ised-isde.canada.ca】 and the job you’re offering meets all of the following requirements:
L81: 
L82:   1. The job is in 【19†National Occupational Classification (NOC) Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities (TEER) categories 0, 1, 2 or 3†noc.esdc.gc.ca】 (high-skilled).
L83:   2. You meet the wage assessment for the job you’re offering.
L84: ### Exemptions
L85: 
L86: #### Open work permits
L87: 
L88: If you hire a temporary worker who has an 【20†open work permit】, you don’t need to submit an offer of employment form or pay the employer compliance fee.
L89: 
L90: An open work permit allows the permit holder to work for any Canadian employer.
L91: 
L92: #### Employer compliance exemptions
L93: 
L94: Some employers don’t need to use the Employer Portal or are exempt from the employer compliance fee.
L95: 
L96: 【21†Find out if you’re exempt】.
L97: 
L98: 【4†Sign in to the Employer Portal 】(opens in a new tab)
L99: ## After you submit an offer of employment
L100: 
L101: After you submit an offer of employment through the Employer Portal, you’ll get an offer of employment number. You must give this 7-digit number to the temporary worker you plan to hire or employ.
L102: 
L103: Once the worker has this number, they can complete and submit the 【22†work permit application】.
L104: 
L105: ## Applying for a work permit
L106: ### Applicants who apply online outside Canada
L107: 
L108: We’ll review the worker’s application to see if they’re 【23†eligible to work in Canada】. If approved, the temporary worker will get
L109: 
L110:   * a port of entry letter of introduction from Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
L111:   * a work permit from a border services officer, if they are still eligible, when they arrive in Canada
L112: ### Applicants who are eligible to apply for or extend their work permit in Canada
L113: 
L114: If their application is approved, we’ll mail them a work permit. They won’t receive a port of entry letter.
L115: ### Applicants who are eligible to apply at a port of entry
L116: 
L117: In Canada work permit applicants: new rules about applying at a port of entry
L118: 
L119: Most foreign nationals already in Canada can 【24†no longer apply for a work permit at a port of entry】. You must apply online for
L120: 
L121:   * your 【25†initial work permit】
L122:   * your 【26†work permit extension】
L123: 
L124: If you’re outside of Canada, you 【27†may still be eligible to apply for a work permit】 when you arrive at a port of entry.
L125: If you’re in Canada and leave as a worker on 【28†maintained status】, you’ll lose your ability to work when you return. This means you can’t work until your application is approved.
L126: 
L127: Some applicants are 【29†eligible to apply at a port of entry】. At the port of entry, the border services officer will assess if the worker both
L128: 
L129:   * meets the requirements of the work permit category they’re applying for
L130:   * 【30†is admissible to Canada】
L131: If the border services officer is satisfied that all requirements are met, they’ll issue a work permit.
L132: ## Other things to tell your temporary worker
L133:   * Make sure your temporary worker has the 【31†right entry document†ircc.canada.ca】. They will either need a 【32†visitor visa】 or an 【33†electronic travel authorization】 (eTA) to enter Canada. These documents are issued with the work permit if you are coming to Canada from another country.
L134:   * Depending on the type of work they’ll do in Canada and where they lived the previous year, temporary workers may have to undergo a 【34†medical examination】 during the application process.
L135:   * Some countries have requirements that citizens must meet before leaving the country. They may need an exit visa or other documents related to their Canadian employment. Temporary workers should check with their government authorities to find out what the requirements are before they attempt to leave.
L136:   * Make sure you hire someone with a valid work permit who follows the 【35†conditions listed on their work permit†www.ircc.canada.ca】.
L137:   * Give the temporary worker information on 【36†their rights as a worker in Canada】.

L38: # Who can apply
L39: ## Who can participate
L40: 
L41: To participate in International Experience Canada (IEC), your country or territory of citizenship must have a youth mobility agreement (YMA) with Canada.
L42: 
L43: Some countries only allow you to participate once. Others allow you to participate twice, but in different categories. Because each country is different, you should check your country’s eligibility requirements.
L44: 
L45: Young Professionals employment eligibility requirements
L46: The job you’re offered must count toward your “professional development.” To count, the job must be classified under Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities (TEER) category 0, 1, 2 or 3 of the 【14†NOC】.
L47: 
L48: A TEER 4 job may qualify if it’s in your field of study. When you apply, you’ll need to submit your 【15†post-secondary】
L49: 
L50:   * diploma
L51:   * certificate or
L52:   * degree
L53: ### You can’t participate with a refugee travel document
L54: 
L55: You’re not eligible to participate in IEC if you hold a refugee travel document from any country.

L51:   * your 【17†port-of-entry (POE) letter of introduction (LOI)†ircc.canada.ca】
L52:   * 【13†proof of health insurance】
L53:   * 【14†proof of funds】
L54:   * a ticket for your departure from Canada or sufficient funds to purchase such a ticket
L55:   * copies of the documents you provided in your work permit application
L56: You’ll get a work permit if the border services officer is satisfied that you are 【18†admissible to Canada】.
L57: 
L58: If the officer isn’t satisfied, you may be asked to return to your country on the next flight at your own expense.
L59: ## Proof of health insurance
L60: 
L61: The border services officer may ask you for proof of health insurance.
L62: 
L63: You may be refused entry if you don’t have insurance.
L64: 
L65: Your insurance must cover:
L66: 
L67:   * medical care,
L68:   * hospitalization
L69:   * repatriation (returning you to your country in the event of severe illness, injury or death)
L70: When you arrive at the port of entry, you must have health insurance valid for your entire stay in Canada. Having a valid provincial health card is not enough. Repatriation isn’t covered by provincial health insurance.
L71: 
L72: If your insurance policy is valid for less than your expected stay, we’ll issue you a work permit that expires at the same time as your insurance.
L73: 
L74: If this happens, you won’t be able to apply to extend your work permit at a later date.
L75: ## Proof of funds
L76: 
L77: The border services officer may also ask for proof of funds.
L78: 
L79: You must present a statement of your bank account issued no more than 1 week before your departure for Canada. It must clearly show that you have enough money to support yourself for the first 3 months of your stay in Canada (the equivalent of CAN$2,500).
L80: 
L81: If you’re an unpaid International Co-op (Internship) participant, you may need to show proof of additional financial resources to cover expenses for your entire stay.
L82: If you 【19†arrive in Canada with the equivalent of CAN$10,000 or more†www.cbsa-asfc.gc.ca】, you must tell the border services officer. If you don’t, you could be fined or put in prison. These funds could be in the form of:
L83: 
L84:   * cash
L85:   * securities in bearer form (for example, stocks, bonds, debentures, treasury bills)
L86:   * bankers’ drafts, cheques, travellers’ cheques or money orders
L87: ## Review your work permit
L88: 
L89: Check your work permit carefully before leaving the port of entry. Make sure you understand all the information on the permit.
L90: 
L91: If you think there’s a mistake on your work permit, tell the border services officer right away.
L92: ### What to look for on your work permit
L93: 
L94: Make sure your name is spelled correctly.
L95: 
L96: Check the expiry date shown under the “Valid until” box.
L97: 
L98: Your work permit won’t be valid past:
L99: 
L100:   * the amount of time indicated in the agreement between Canada and your country
L101:   * the expiry date of your passport
L102:   * the expiry date of your biometrics
L103:   * the expiry date of your health insurance
L104:   * the end date of your work contract (Young Professionals and International Co-op (Internship) participants)
L105: Check for medical restrictions. If you passed an immigration medical exam, you shouldn’t have medical restrictions on your work permit.
L106: 
L107: Working Holiday participants
L108: 
L109: Your work permit should show:
L110: 
L111:   * “open” employer, and
L112:   * “unknown” location.
L113: 
L114: Open employer and unknown employment location means you have an 【20†open work permit】.
L115: 
L116: As long as your work permit is valid, there are no restrictions on:
L117:   * how long you can work, or
L118:   * how many hours you can work.
L119: Young Professionals or International Co-op (Internship) participants
L120: 
L121: The validity period of your work permit normally matches the period your employer requested in your job offer.
L122: 
L123: Your work permit should indicate the name and location of your employer.
L124: 
L125: You can only work in the location and for the employer specified in your work permit. The employer’s name and location are based on the offer of employment submitted.

L44: ## Eligibility requirements
L45: 
L46: You can come to Canada to study if you
L47:   * are enrolled at a 【16†DLI】
L48:   * prove you have 【17†enough money】 to pay for
L49:     * your tuition fees
L50:     * living expenses for yourself and any family members who come with you to Canada and
L51:     * return transportation for yourself and any family members who come with you to Canada
L52:   * obey the law, have no criminal record and get a 【18†police certificate】 (if required)
L53:   * are in good health and get a 【19†medical exam】 (if required) and
L54:   * prove to an officer that you will leave Canada when your study permit expires
L55: ## Your responsibilities as a student
L56: 
L57: While studying in Canada you must
L58: 
L59:   * make progress towards completing your program
L60:   * respect any conditions listed on your study permit
L61:   * stop studying if you no longer meet the requirements
L62: 
L63: Depending on your case, there may be conditions on your study permit such as
L64:   * if you’re allowed to work in Canada
L65:   * the specific date you must leave Canada
L66:   * where you can study (a specific DLI listed on your permit)
L67:     * You need to follow our instructions if you want to 【20†change schools at the post-secondary level】.
L68:   * whether you need an immigration medical examination
L69: ## Post-graduation work permit
L70: 
L71: You may be able to stay and work in Canada after you graduate by getting a 【21†post-graduation work permit (PGWP)】. PGWP eligibility depends on several requirements, including when you submit your study permit application. If you’re interested, check the requirements before you submit your study permit application.
L72: 
L73: Check if the 【22†DLI you choose】 offers PGWP-eligible programs.
L74: 
L75: PGWP eligibility requirements
L76: 
L77: PGWP has 3 sets of eligibility requirements:
L78:   * general eligibility requirements,
L79:     * For example, you must complete an eligible program of study at 【22†a PGWP-eligible DLI】
L80:   * eligibility requirements based on your study program
L81:     * These may include language or field of study requirements.
L82:   * eligibility requirements based on your physical location
L83: 
L84: If your level of study has a field of study requirement, you should make sure your program meets the eligibility requirement before you submit your study permit application.
L85: 【23†Learn more about PGWP eligibility requirements】.

L36: # Proof of financial support
L37: 
L38: You must prove that you have enough money, without working in Canada, to pay for all the following:
L39: 
L40:   * tuition fees for the course or program of studies
L41:   * living expenses for yourself and the family members who come with you while you’re in Canada
L42:   * transportation to and from Canada for yourself and your accompanying family members
L43: ## How to show you meet the financial capacity requirements
L44: 
L45: You must provide us with documents that prove you have the required funds available for all the costs listed above. This means that
L46:   1. you must show you have enough financial resources for the first year of your studies
L47:   2. for programs more than a year long, you must also tell us how you plan to pay for the full duration of your studies
L48:      * For example, you can show proof that your scholarship is more than a year long, proof that your parents are employed, etc.
L49: 
L50: We’ll assess the amount of funds you have and their source, and confirm that you have funds available to you throughout the full duration of your studies.
L51: Common documents that can be used to show proof of funds
L52: 
L53: The documents below are examples of documents you can use as proof of funds.
L54: 
L55:   * This is not a complete list. There may be other types of documents you can provide as proof instead.
L56:   * You don’t need to provide all of these documents, but you do need to give enough proof to show that you meet all the financial capacity requirements.
L57: Tuition and study costs
L58: 
L59: For example, you can use
L60:   * proof you paid for the first year of your tuition and housing fees, such as a receipt from your designated learning institution
L61:     * This must be accompanied by other documents proving you have 【13†sufficient funds to cover living expenses】 and transportation costs.
L62:   * proof of a student or education loan from a bank
L63:   * proof of a scholarship or that you’re in a Government of Canada–funded educational program
L64:     * If your scholarship only covers tuition, you must provide other documents proving you have 【13†sufficient funds to cover living expenses】 and transportation costs.
L65: Employment and other financial support
L66: For example, you can use
L67:   * pay stubs from recent employment
L68:   * a letter from the person or institution giving you money that includes
L69:     * their employment or occupation (a letter from the employer, pay stubs, etc.)
L70:     * their relationship to you
L71:     * the number of their dependants, if they have any
L72:     * the amount of their support
L73:   * proof of the relationship to the person or institution giving you money and evidence of the financial support they will provide
L74:     * This must include a copy of their identification photo or proof of their business registration.
L75: Banking and other income
L76: For example, you can use
L77:   * proof of a Canadian bank account in your name if you’ve transferred money to Canada
L78:   * a 【14†guaranteed investment certificate】 from a Canadian financial institution
L79:   * your bank statements (for your Canadian or foreign bank account) for the past 6 months, including the month you submitted your application or the month prior
L80:     * This must include documentation to show the source of the income (employment income, savings transfers, etc.) in the bank statements.
L81:   * financial documents related to a pension plan
L82:   * proof of income from rental properties
L83: 【6†Other documents】 may also be required. Check the visa office instructions for your country or region for local requirements.
L84: 
L85: If your country uses foreign exchange controls, you must prove that you’ll be allowed to export funds for all of your expenses.

L43: ## Your study permit conditions
L44: 
L45: As a study permit holder, you need to meet a number of conditions. If you don’t meet these conditions, you may lose your student status and study permit. You may also have to leave Canada.
L46: 
L47: As a study permit holder, you must
L48:   * be enrolled at a 【15†designated learning institution (DLI)】, unless you’re exempt
L49:   * show you’re actively pursuing your studies, unless you’re exempt, by
L50:     * being enrolled full-time or part-time during each academic semester (excluding regularly scheduled breaks)
L51:       * If you’re studying in Quebec, make sure to 【16†check the province’s specific requirements†www.quebec.ca】.
L52:     * making progress towards completing your program’s courses and
L53:     * not taking 【17†authorized leaves longer than 150 days】 from your study program
L54:   * apply to extend your study permit to change post-secondary schools
L55:   * end your studies if you no longer meet the requirements of being a student and
L56:   * leave Canada when your permit expires
L57: ### Other study permit conditions you may need to follow
L58: 
L59: You may have other conditions listed on your study permit. You must follow these conditions, which could include
L60: 
L61:   * the level of studies
L62:   * if you’re allowed to 【18†work on or off campus as a student】 in Canada
L63:   * if you need to report for medical procedures
L64:   * if you’re allowed to travel within Canada, and
L65:   * the date you must stop studying.
L66: #### If you’ve deferred your enrolment
L67: 
L68: If you’ve deferred your enrolment and the DLI that issued your letter of acceptance is de-designated before you start studying, you cannot start studying at that school.
L69: 
L70:   * If you’re in Canada with a valid study permit, you’ll need to
L71:     * apply to and be accepted at a new DLI
L72:     * apply to extend your study permit
L73:   * If your study permit has been approved but not issued yet
L74:     * we’ll send you a request to provide a new letter of acceptance from a new DLI
L75: ### What counts as an authorized leave from your studies?
L76: 
L77: There are a few cases where you may be able to take a leave of up to a maximum of 150 days from your program of studies and still be considered to be actively pursuing your studies.
L78: 
L79: You don’t need to tell us if you’re taking an authorized leave. However, if we ask for it, you must provide proof that your leave is
L80: 
L81:   * authorized by your DLI and
L82:   * no longer than 150 days
L83: 
L84: It counts as authorized leave if
L85:   * your school has authorized a leave from your study program for
L86:     * medical reasons or pregnancy
L87:     * family emergency
L88:     * death or serious illness of a family member
L89:     * any other type of leave your school authorizes
L90:   * your school has closed permanently or because of a strike
L91:   * you’ve changed schools
L92:   * you or your school deferred your program start date
L93:     * In this case, you must start your studies the next semester, even if it starts sooner than 150 days, and get an updated letter of acceptance.
L94: You can’t work on or off campus during an authorized leave from your study program, even if your study permit says you’re allowed to work in Canada.
L95: 
L96: If your school is temporarily closed because of a strike, and you’re authorized to work on or off campus, you remain authorized to work up to a maximum of 150 days.
L97: ## How to prove that you meet your conditions
L98: 
L99: We might ask you to prove you’re meeting your conditions:
L100: 
L101:   * as part of a random check
L102:   * if we have reason to believe you’re not meeting them
L103: 
L104: We might ask you for:
L105:   * official documents from your school confirming:
L106:     * your enrolment status
L107:     * the reason for and start date of any leave you’ve taken
L108:     * the date you withdrew from a school or study program
L109:     * the date you were suspended or dismissed from a school or study program
L110:     * the date you stopped studying at the school
L111:   * official transcripts
L112:   * references from people who know you
L113:   * proof from a medical professional confirming the medical need for a leave from your study program
L114:   * document confirming your school has closed and no longer offers your study program
L115:   * any other document an officer finds relevant
L116: ### What happens if you don’t meet your study permit conditions
L117: 
L118: If we find you haven’t met your study permit conditions, we may ask you to leave Canada. You might also have to wait 6 months before you can apply for a new study permit (or for a visitor visa or work permit in Canada).
L119: 
L120: The outcome of any future applications you submit could be impacted if you do either of the following:
L121: 
L122:   * you don’t follow your study permit conditions
L123:   * you work or study in a way we haven’t authorized
L124: ## People who are exempt from study permit conditions
L125: 
L126: If you meet all of your 【12†study permit conditions】, you get to keep your study permit and status as a student. However, some study permit holders are exempt from certain conditions.
L127: 
L128: You don’t need to prove that you’re enrolled at a DLI or that you’re actively pursuing your studies if:
L129:   * you or a family member (spouse or dependent child) has made a refugee claim in Canada that hasn’t yet been decided on
L130:   * you have refugee status in Canada
L131:   * you or a family member (spouse or dependent child) are a Convention refugee or a humanitarian-protected person
L132:   * you’re an accredited representative of another country, the United Nations, or any international organization of which Canada is a member, or you’re the staff or family member (spouse or dependent child) of this person
L133:   * you or your family member (spouse or dependent child) is a member of a foreign armed force in Canada on official duties
L134:   * you already have a study permit and have suddenly become impoverished for reasons beyond your control and temporarily can’t continue your studies
L135:   * you’re studying in Canada under a student exchange agreement between Canada and another country
L136:   * you or your family member (spouse or dependent child) works in Canada:

L141:   * you or your family member (spouse or dependent child) have a passport from the United States and are working temporarily in Canada on behalf of the United States government

L27: # Changing schools or programs as an international student
L28: 
L29: Find out what to do if you’re changing your designated learning institution (DLI) or study program.
L30: ## On this page
L31: 
L32:   * 【5†Find the right process for your situation】
L33:   * 【6†Changing your DLI in Quebec】
L34:   * 【7†Changing the DLI on your study permit application while it's still in progress】
L35:   * 【8†Changing your DLI if you’re outside Canada】
L36:   * 【9†Changing your DLI while on a student work placement】
L37:   * 【10†If you change schools without telling us】
L38: ## Find the right process for your situation
L39: 
L40: If you’re changing schools or programs, what you need to do depends on your situation.
L41: 
L42: Select the option that matches your situation:
L43: 
L44:   * 【11†I’m changing schools.】
L45:   * 【12†I’m changing programs or levels of study at the same school.】
L46: 
L47: What will you be doing?
L48:   * 【13†I’m changing schools but staying at the same level of study within the post-secondary level (for example: staying at the bachelor’s level).】
L49:   * 【13†I’m changing schools within the post-secondary level (for example: from the bachelor level to the master’s level).】
L50:   * 【13†I’m changing schools because I need to complete prerequisite courses.】
L51:   * 【14†I’m changing schools because I’m enrolled in a joint program that results in a single credential.】
L52:   * 【14†I’m changing schools within the primary or secondary level.】
L53:   * 【15†I’m changing schools because I’m moving from the secondary level to the post-secondary level.】
L54: What will you be doing?
L55: 
L56:   * 【16†I’ll be changing programs of study at the post-secondary level.】
L57:   * 【14†I’ll be moving from the primary level to the secondary level.】
L58: ## You need to extend your study permit
L59: 
L60: You need to get a new study permit by applying to extend your current one before you can start studying at your new DLI.
L61: 
L62: The school you plan to change to must also be a DLI. Before committing to changing schools and applying for a study permit extension, make sure to check that your new school is on the 【17†DLI list】.
L63: ### Documents you need
L64: 
L65: When you apply, make sure to include
L66:   * a letter explaining why you’re changing schools
L67:   * a new, valid 【18†provincial attestation letter or territorial attestation letter (PAL or TAL)】, unless you meet one of the exceptions
L68:     * Make sure to get a new PAL or TAL before you submit your application.
L69:     * This is a new requirement as of January 22, 2025.
L70:   * documents that prove that you meet 【19†the criteria below】, if you believe you meet the criteria to begin studying at the new DLI while your new application is in progress
L71: If you already applied but didn’t include the required documents
L72: 
L73: If you submitted an application and you didn’t include the above documents, you can submit them using the 【20†IRCC web form】.
L74: #### When you can start studying at your new DLI
L75: 
L76: You can start studying at your new school while waiting for a decision on your study permit extension application only if you meet all the following criteria:
L77:   * You haven’t left Canada since receiving your letter of acceptance (LOA) from the new DLI.
L78:   * You continue to meet the conditions of your previous study permit.
L79:   * Before you completed your course or program of study, the DLI you were studying at
L80:     * closed
L81:     * discontinued your course or program of study
L82:     * was placed on the suspension list
L83:     * lost its designated status
L84: If you do not meet these criteria, you should plan to apply for and get your extended study permit for your new DLI before finishing your studies at your current DLI.
L85: #### Faster processing for students changing schools New
L86: 
L87: Get your study permit extension application processed in 60 days if you’re changing to a new post-secondary DLI. Make sure to follow our instructions when you apply.
L88: 
L89: You must tell us you’re changing schools when you apply online by selecting “Yes” to one of the following questions (as applicable):
L90:   * Are you a student residing in Canada who is changing your designated learning institution?
L91:   * Is your accompanying family member a student residing in Canada who is changing their designated learning institution?
L92: 
L93: 【21†Apply for your study permit extension】
L94: ### You can keep studying with your current study permit
L95: 
L96: You don’t need to apply for a study permit extension if your current study permit is still valid, unless your study permit has conditions that limit you from doing so.
L97: ### You need a new study permit
L98: 
L99: If you already have a study permit
L100: 
L101: You need to get a new study permit by applying to extend your current one.
L102: 
L103: You can continue your studies at the post-secondary level while waiting for a decision on your new study permit application even if your study permit has the condition “Going to primary or secondary school”.
L104: 
L105: If you don’t already have a study permit
L106: If you’re attending secondary school while holding a visitor record, you need to apply for and be approved for a study permit before you start your studies at a post-secondary school.
L107: 
L108: 【21†Apply for your study permit extension】
L109: ### You may need to extend your study permit
L110: 
L111: You can keep studying at your DLI with your current study permit as long as you still meet your 【22†study permit conditions】.
L112: 
L113: If you need to extend your study permit to attend your new program, you may need to submit a new 【18†provincial attestation letter (PAL) or territorial attestation letter (TAL).】
L114: You can start studying in your new program while waiting for a decision on your study permit extension. If your application is refused, you must stop studying immediately.
L115: 
L116: 【21†Apply for your study permit extension】
L117: ## Changing your DLI in Quebec
L118: 
L119: 【23†With few exceptions】, if you’re moving to a school in Quebec, you must get an attestation of issuance of your 【24†Quebec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ)】 and submit this with your study permit application.
L120: 
L121: If you’re changing between schools that are vocational training centres, you don’t need to apply for a new study permit, but you need a new CAQ.
L122: You should contact the 【25†Ministère de l’Immigration, de la Francisation et de l’Intégration†www.quebec.ca】 if you’re already studying in Quebec and want to change your
L123: 
L124:   * educational institution
L125:   * level of study
L126: ## Changing the DLI on your study permit application while it’s still in progress
L127: 
L128: You can tell us that you would like to change the DLI in your application by submitting a new letter of acceptance and a 【18†provincial or territorial attestation】 letter (if needed) in the 【20†IRCC web form】.

L36: # Who can apply
L37: 
L38: To be eligible for a post-graduation work permit (PGWP), you must meet all eligibility requirements.
L39: 
L40: Eligibility requirements include
L41:   * 【12†general eligibility】
L42:   * 【13†eligibility requirements based on study program】
L43:     * Study program requirements include both
L44:       * proof of language skills
L45:       * field of study requirements (if applicable)
L46:   * 【14†eligibility requirements based on physical location】
L47:     * inside Canada graduates
L48:     * outside Canada graduates
L49:   * 【15†field of study requirements (if applicable)】
L50: ## General eligibility
L51: 
L52: You meet the general eligibility requirement to apply for a PGWP if
L53:   * you completed a program of study at a PGWP-eligible 【16†designated learning institution】 that was at least 8 months long (or 900 hours for Quebec programs)
L54:   * you maintained full-time status as a student in Canada during each semester of your study program
L55:     * You may study part-time during your final semester.
L56:   * you apply for your PGWP within 180 days of confirmation that you completed your program of study
L57:   * your study permit was valid at some point during the 180 days after you completed your program of study
L58: 【17†Check the special cases to learn if exceptions to the general eligibility requirements apply to your situation】.
L59: 
L60: Special cases
L61: 
L62: You may also be eligible to apply for a PGWP if you’re in one of the special case groups.
L63: 
L64: Accelerated programs
L65: 
L66: If you complete your study program in less time than the normal length of the program, you may be eligible for a PGWP that is valid for the full length of your program.
L67: For example, if you complete a 1-year study program in 8 months, you may be able to get a PGWP valid for 1 year.
L68: 
L69: Distance learning
L70: ### Distance learning from outside of Canada
L71: 
L72: You can complete up to 100% of your studies online from outside Canada between March 2020 and August 31, 2022, because of a temporary COVID-19 policy. This temporary policy was in place until August 31, 2022.
L73: 
L74: You’re eligible for this temporary policy if you meet all of the following criteria:
L75:   * You’re enrolled in a PGWP-eligible program.
L76:   * You were outside Canada and did not travel to Canada because of the COVID-19 pandemic, but were still able to take online courses.
L77:   * You began a program of study between March 2020 and August 31, 2022, or your program was already in progress in March 2020.
L78:   * You applied for a study permit before starting your program and the application was approved before your program ended.
L79:     * You can count the time you spent studying after you submitted your initial study permit application, even if it’s refused, as long as you submit another application that is eventually approved before you finish your study program.
L80:   * You meet all other PGWP eligibility criteria.
L81: This temporary policy changed as of September 1, 2022.
L82: 
L83: To find out if these changes apply to you and how, check the date
L84: 
L85:   * that you started your program of study
L86:   * on the study permit application receipt that we sent you
L87: 
L88: Whichever date comes first is the lock-in date that applies to you. Next, check the rules for distance learning for your lock-in date.
L89: 
L90: Lock-in date between September 1, 2022, and August 31, 2024
L91:   * You must complete at least 50% of your program within Canada (online or in class).
L92:   * The time spent studying online from outside of Canada before August 31, 2024, will count toward the length of your PGWP as long as it constitutes less than 50% of your program of study.
L93: Lock-in date on or after September 1, 2024
L94: 
L95:   * You must complete at least 50% of your program in class within Canada.
L96:   * The time spent studying outside of Canada will be deducted from the length of your PGWP.
L97: What doesn’t count toward the length of your PGWP
L98: 
L99: You can’t count the following time toward the length of a PGWP:
L100: 
L101:   * time spent studying online from outside Canada after August 31, 2024
L102:   * time spent studying before we receive your study permit application
L103: #### Distance learning from inside Canada
L104: 
L105: If your courses were moved online due to the pandemic, the time you spent studying online from within Canada until August 31, 2024 , still counts toward the length of your PGWP.
L106: 
L107: The temporary policy change for in-Canada students studying online ended on August 31, 2024.
L108: 
L109: Curriculum licensing agreements (public-private partnership)
L110: These agreements allow students to graduate from a program that was delivered by a private career college on behalf of a public PGWP-eligible institution. These programs are not PGWP-eligible in most cases (check exceptions below).
L111: 
L112: Exception 1: Curriculum licensing agreements within the same province
L113: If you began a program of study at a private college being delivered on behalf of a public college in the same province on or before May 15, 2024, you may be eligible for a PGWP. You must also meet all other PGWP eligibility criteria.
L114: 
L115: If you began one of these programs, after May 15, 2024, you’re, not eligible for a PGWP.
L116: 
L117: Exception 2: Curriculum licensing agreements between provinces
L118: If you began a program of study at a private college being delivered on behalf of a public college in another province on or before January 31, 2023, you may be eligible for a PGWP. You must also meet all other PGWP eligibility criteria.
L119: 
L120: If you began one of these programs after February 1, 2023, you’re not eligible for a PGWP.
L121: 
L122: Taking leave from your studies
L123: 
L124: You may not be eligible for a PGWP if
L125:   * you take an unauthorized leave from your study program and
L126:   * we find that you didn’t meet the conditions of your study permit by taking this leave
L127: 
L128: There are a few cases where you may be able to take an authorized leave of up to 150 days from your study program and still meet the conditions of your study permit. You need to provide proof that your DLI authorized the leave when you apply for a PGWP.
L129: 
L130: 【18†Find out what counts as an authorized leave from your studies】.
L131: 
L132: Transfers between schools
L133: If you transferred between 【16†designated learning institutions (DLIs)】
L134: 
L135: The length of your studies must be at least 8 months for you to be eligible.
L136: 
L137: If you transferred from a non-DLI to a DLI
L138: 
L139: Only the time you spent studying at the DLI will be counted. You must spend at least 8 months at the DLI to be eligible for a PGWP.
L140: 
L141: Canadian study programs with an overseas component
L142: If your study program has an overseas component, you may be eligible for a PGWP as long as you earn a credit from a Canadian school for it. The PGWP will only be valid for the length of the time you studied in Canada.
L143: 
L144: Graduates of certain Quebec schools
L145: 
L146: When you apply for a PGWP, you must include
L147:   * an official letter from the school that confirms the length of the study program and the program code, and either
L148:     * the certificate or official document that confirms that you completed your program or
L149:     * an official transcript from a Quebec school board or recognized private school
L150: Who’s not eligible for a PGWP
L151: 
L152: You aren’t eligible for a PGWP if you
L153:   * already received a PGWP
L154:   * studied English or French as a second language
L155:   * took general interest or self-improvement courses
L156:   * completed a non-credit program of study (except for a flight school program)
L157:   * received funding or a scholarship from GAC that requires you to return to your home country after graduation
L158:   * completed over 50% of your study program through distance learning (online courses, e-learning or correspondence)
L159:     * Note: 【19†You may still be eligible for a PGWP】 if you could only study online from outside Canada because of COVID-19.
L160:   * completed a study program at a non-Canadian institution located in Canada
L161:   * completed a course or program of study at a DLI that is not PGWP-eligible
L162:     * This includes programs delivered on behalf of a 【16†PGWP-eligible DLI】 through a 【20†curriculum licensing agreement】 (also known as public private partnerships, or P3s). 【17†Check the special cases for exceptions】.
L163: ## Eligibility requirements based on study program
L164: 
L165: If you graduated with a bachelor’s degree, master’s degree or doctoral degree
L166: ### Language requirement:
L167: 
L168: You must prove 【21†your English or French language skills】 with a minimum level of Canadian Language Benchmarks (CLB) 7 in English or Niveaux de competence linguistique canadiens (NCLC) 7 in French in all 4 language areas.
L169: 
L170: 【7†Find out what your language level is based on your language test results】.
L171: 
L172: If you submitted your PGWP application before November 1, 2024
L173: 
L174: You don’t need to meet the language requirement for your program.
L175: #### Field of study requirement:
L176: 
L177: There are no field of study requirements for graduates with a bachelor’s degree, master’s degree or doctoral degree.
L178: 
L179: If you graduated from any other university program
L180: #### Language requirement:
L181: 
L182: You must 【21†prove your English or French language skills】 with a minimum level of Canadian Language Benchmarks (CLB) 7 in English or Niveaux de competence linguistique canadiens (NCLC) 7 in French in all 4 language areas.
L183: 
L184: 【7†Find out what your language level is based on your language test results】.

L34: # Get the right documents
L35: 
L36: You need these documents to apply for a post-graduation work permit (PGWP):
L37:   * 【10†proof that you’ve completed your studies】
L38:   * 【11†proof that you were enrolled in full-time studies for a program that was 8 months or longer】
L39:   * 【12†for applications submitted on or after November 1, 2024, proof of language ability (if applicable)】
L40:   * 【13†for graduates who apply for their study permit on or after November 1, 2024, proof that you graduated in an eligible field of study (if applicable)】
L41:   * 【14†proof of upfront medical exam (if applicable)】
L42: We may request other documents once we receive your application.
L43: ## Proof that you completed your studies
L44: 
L45: When you apply for your PGWP, you need one of the following to prove you’ve completed your studies:
L46: 
L47:   * a degree, diploma or certificate from a credit-earning program (except flight school programs)
L48:     * A credit-earning program gives official credits toward a degree, diploma or certificate at a college or university.
L49:   * an official letter from your school
L50:   * an official transcript or a copy of your transcript from your school’s website
L51: Your proof must be from a PGWP-eligible designated learning institution (DLI) and program, and you must 【15†meet all program requirements for PGWP eligibility】.
L52: ## Proof that you were enrolled in full-time studies
L53: 
L54: When you apply for your PGWP, you must prove that you were enrolled in full-time studies. You can prove this by submitting
L55: 
L56:   * an official transcript issued by your DLI
L57:   * a copy of your official transcript from your DLI’s website
L58: ## Proof of language results
L59: 
L60: If you apply on or after November 1, 2024, you must provide proof of English or French language skills. The only exception is if you graduate from a PGWP-eligible flight school.
L61: 
L62: Your PGWP document checklist will list the proof of language results as an optional document. You must include this proof with your application if it’s a requirement for your study program.
L63: 
L64: Your language score requirement is based on your 【15†study program】.
L65: Language tests should be taken in person. You must demonstrate your skill in each of the following abilities:
L66: 
L67:   * reading
L68:   * writing
L69:   * listening
L70:   * speaking
L71: 
L72: Your test results must be less than 2 years old when you submit your application. We accept language test results from these tests:
L73: 
L74: English  | French
L75: --- | ---
L76: 【16†CELPIP: Canadian English Language Proficiency Index Program†www.celpip.ca】
L77:   * You should take the CELPIP-General test.
L78:  | 【17†TEF Canada: Test d’évaluation de français†www.lefrancaisdesaffaires.fr】
L79: 【18†IELTS: International English Language Testing System†www.ielts.org】
L80: 
L81:   * You should take the IELTS General Training option.

L36: # Field of study requirement
L37: 
L38: Depending on your 【12†study program】, you may need to meet a field of study requirement to be eligible for a post-graduation work permit (PGWP).
L39: 
L40: Who doesn’t need to meet the field of study requirement
L41: 
L42: You don’t need to meet the field of study requirement if one of the following applies to you:
L43:   * You submitted your PGWP application before November 1, 2024, regardless of level of study.
L44:   * You graduated from a PGWP-eligible flight school.
L45:   * You graduated with a bachelor’s degree, master’s degree or doctoral degree.
L46:   * You applied for a study permit before November 1, 2024.
L47: 
L48: If you don’t meet one of the exceptions above, use the table below to check if your program is eligible for a PGWP.
L49:

L58: ## How to meet the field of study requirement
L59: 
L60: You must graduate from a program that’s on the list of currently eligible 【18†Classification of Instructional Programs (CIP) codes】 when you submit your
L61: 
L62:   * study permit application or
L63:   * PGWP application
L64: Eligible fields of study are linked to certain jobs in long-term shortage in Canada and can change based on the needs of the Canadian labour market. If your CIP code is not on the list of currently eligible codes when you apply for a PGWP, it may still be eligible based on when you submitted your study permit application.
L65: 
L66: What’s a CIP code?
L67: 
L68: A CIP code is a number we use to classify post-secondary education programs according to the field of study.
L69: For PGWP eligibility, we use 6-digit CIP codes based on the 【19†CIP Canada 2021†www.statcan.gc.ca】 (opens in a new tab).
L70: 
L71: To find your program’s CIP code, you can
L72:   * check your designated learning institution’s (DLI) website
L73:     * Most DLIs have information about PGWP eligibility and CIP codes on their website.
L74:   * contact your DLI
L75:     * Contact your DLI for more information about the program and applicable 6-digit CIP codes if you have any questions.
L76:   * search the 【20†Statistics Canada CIP classification catalogue†www23.statcan.gc.ca】 and find the 6-digit code that’s most applicable
L77:     * Search by keyword or by navigating through the available links in the main table.
L78:     * Program titles can be broad. Read the description, illustrative examples and exceptions found on the individual results to make sure your program matches.
L79: ## Check if your CIP code is eligible
L80: 
L81: To meet the field of study requirement, your CIP code must be on the list of currently eligible CIP codes when you submit either your study permit application or your PGWP application.

L26: ### Biometrics and the application process
L27: 
L28: 【5†Image: Image that represents the different stages of the application process and biometrics.】
L29: 
L30: We refer to your fingerprints and photo as biometrics. We collect biometrics for most applications. Find out what happens from when you submit your application to when you get to Canada and where biometrics fits in the process.
L31: #### 1. Apply for your visitor visa, study permit or work permit
L32: 
L33: If you want to visit, study or work in Canada, make sure you’re eligible to apply. Use our application guides to help fill out your application properly, then submit your application.
L34: 
L35: Avoid processing delays by sending us a 【6†complete application†www.ircc.canada.ca】.
L36: #### 2. Get your fingerprints and photo taken
L37: 
L38: If you’re between 14 and 79 years old, you probably need to give your fingerprints and photo (biometrics).You only need to give your biometrics once every 10 years to make repeat trips to Canada easier.
L39:   * You must pay the 【7†biometrics fee】 when you submit your application. Otherwise you may experience delays.
L40:   * Get this done as soon as you get the letter from us that tells you to give biometrics.
L41:   * You have 30 days to do this from the date on the letter.
L42: 
L43: Find out 【8†who needs to give†ircc.canada.ca】, 【9†how to give】, and 【10†where to give your biometrics】.
L44: #### 3. We process your application
L45: 
L46: After we get your biometrics, we start processing your application. See 【11†how long it takes to process your application.】
L47: 
L48: If we need more information from you, we’ll contact you.
L49: 
L50: #### 4. We make a decision on your application
L51: 
L52: When we finish reviewing your application, we let you know if you’re approved to come to Canada. If you are, we issue your documents.
L53: 
L54: If your application is refused, we send you a letter that tells you why.
L55: #### 5. You travel to Canada (if you’re approved)
L56: 
L57: Make sure you travel with the documents we gave you. This includes travel documents like a visitor visa, study or work permits or an eTA (electronically linked to your passport).
L58: 
L59: Airline staff and border service officers at ports of entry will ask to see your travel documents. If you don’t have them, you may not be able to board your flight to Canada.
L60: 
L61: Make sure children under 18 travel with the 【12†right documents】.
L62: #### 6. We check your identity when you arrive in Canada
L63: 
L64: When you arrive, we check your identity to make sure that you are the same person who was approved to travel to Canada. We may use your biometrics to do this.
L65: 
L66: If we can’t verify your identity, you may be detained by a border services officer. These officers help protect the health and safety of Canadians.
L67: If the officer determines that you’re not admissible to Canada, you won’t be allowed to enter Canada. If you came by air, you’ll have to take a return flight to where you came from.
L68: #### 7. You’re allowed to enter Canada
L69: 
L70: If you pass the identity check and meet the 【13†entry requirements】, the border services officer stamps your passport and lets you know how long you can stay in Canada. You’re normally allowed to stay in Canada for up to six months.
L71: 
L72: Children under 18 must meet the same entry requirements as adults. The border services officer may ask minor children to show 【12†other documents】 depending on whether the child is travelling alone or with someone.
L73: ### Basic entry requirements
L74: 
L75: You must meet some basic requirements to enter Canada. You must:
L76:   * have a valid travel document, like a passport
L77:   * be in good health
L78:   * have no criminal or immigration-related convictions
L79:   * convince an immigration officer that you have ties—such as a job, home, financial assets or family—that will take you back to your home country
L80:   * convince an immigration officer that you will leave Canada at the end of your visit
L81:   * have enough money for your stay
L82:     * The amount of money you will need depends on how long you will stay and if you will stay in a hotel, or with friends or relatives.
L83: Some people are not admissible to Canada, which means they are not allowed to enter the country. You can be inadmissible for several reasons, including being involved in:
L84: 
L85:   * criminal activity
L86:   * human rights violations
L87:   * organized crime
L88: 
L89: You can also be inadmissible for security, health or financial reasons.
L90: 
L91: 【14†Find out more about inadmissibility】.

L43: ## Work while we process your application
L44: 
L45: You can work full-time until we make a decision on your work permit application if you
L46: 
L47:   * had a 【15†valid study permit】 at the time you submitted your application
L48:   * completed your study program
L49:   * were eligible to 【16†work off campus without a work permit】 while studying and you didn’t work more hours than you were allowed to
L50: ## Valid study permit
L51: 
L52: A study permit that has not expired.
L53: 
L54: If you received the WP-EXT for PGWP (IMM 0127 E) letter
L55: 
L56: You can work until we make a decision on your work permit application even if the validity period of the letter expires. If you need proof of authorization to continue working, you can ask for it using our 【17†web form†ircc.canada.ca】.
L57: If these conditions apply to you and you need to prove to an employer that you’re eligible to work, provide the employer with a 【18†copy of all the required documents†ircc.canada.ca】.
L58: 
L59: If these conditions don’t apply to you, you must wait until your work permit arrives to begin your new job. It’s illegal to work in Canada without authorization.
L60: 
L61: If we refuse your work permit, you must stop working the day we notify you.
L62: ## Get your visitor visa or eTA
L63: 
L64: ### If you apply for your post-graduation work permit from outside Canada
L65: 
L66: We’ll issue you a new visitor visa or electronic travel authorization (eTA) when we approve your post-graduation work permit application.
L67: ### If you apply for your post-graduation work permit from inside Canada
L68: 
L69: If you need a visitor visa to enter Canada, we won’t issue you a new one when we approve your post-graduation work permit application. You need to 【19†apply for a new visitor visa】 separately if your current one is expired and you want to travel outside Canada.
L70: 
L71: If you need an eTA to enter Canada by air, we’ll issue you one when we approve your post-graduation work permit application.
L72: ## Travel outside Canada
L73: 
L74: If you’re in Canada and want to travel outside Canada, you must have a valid visitor visa or eTA. If you don’t have a valid visitor visa or eTA when you return to Canada, you may not be let back into the country (even if you have a valid post-graduation work permit).
L75: If you leave and re-enter Canada after applying for your post-graduation work permit, you can still 【10†work full-time】 while you wait for a decision. Leaving and re-entering Canada doesn’t stop you from working full-time while you wait.
L76: 
L77: When you arrive in Canada, you’ll meet a 【20†border services officer】, who will make sure you meet some basic requirements. To enter Canada, you must
L78:   * have a valid travel document, such as a passport
L79:   * be in good health
L80:   * have no criminal or immigration-related convictions
L81:   * convince an immigration officer that you have ties—such as a job, home, financial assets or family—that will take you back to your home country
L82:   * convince an immigration officer that you’ll leave Canada at the end of your visit
L83:   * have enough money for your stay (and the amount of money you’ll need can vary)
L84:   * have valid results for an immigration medical exam (【21†if you needed one】)
L85:     * Your exam is valid for 12 months from the day you get it.
L86:     * The results must be valid on the day you enter Canada.

L34: # About the post-graduation work permit
L35: 
L36: The post-graduation work permit (PGWP) allows students who have graduated from 【10†eligible designated learning institutions (DLIs)】 to gain valuable Canadian work experience.
L37: 
L38: Graduating from a designated learning institution (DLI) doesn’t automatically make you eligible for a PGWP.
L39: 
L40:   * 【10†Check the DLI list】 to find out which schools have eligible programs.
L41: As of November 1, 2024, the 【6†eligibility requirements】 for a PGWP changed. Most PGWP applicants now need to give proof of language results when they apply.
L42: 
L43: If you submitted your PGWP application before November 1, 2024, or are a flight school graduate, you’re exempt from the new requirements.
L44: ## How long is a post-graduation work permit valid?
L45: 
L46: The length of your PGWP depends on the level and duration of your study program, as well as the 【11†expiry date of your passport】, whichever comes first.
L47: 
L48: For master’s degree programs as of February 15, 2024
L49: 
L50: You can apply for a 3-year PGWP, even if your master’s program was less than 2 years, as long as
L51: 
L52:   * your program was at least 8 months (or 900 hours for Quebec programs) and
L53:   * you meet all other eligibility requirements
L54: This doesn’t apply to certificate or diploma programs.
L55: 
L56: For all other programs If your program was at least 8 months (or 900 hours for Quebec credentials), but less than 2 years
L57: 
L58: We may give you a PGWP that’s valid for up to the same length as your study program.
L59: 
L60: For example, if you completed a 9-month program, we may give you a work permit for up to 9 months.
L61: 
L62: If your program was 2 years or more
L63: 
L64: We may give you a PGWP that’s valid for 3 years.
L65: 
L66: If you completed more than 1 program
L67: You may be able to get a PGWP that combines the length of each program as long as you meet the eligibility requirement for each program.
L68: 
L69: For example, if one of the programs has a higher language requirement, you need to meet the higher requirement to get a PGWP that combines the length of both programs.
L70: 
L71: Each of the programs you completed must be
L72: 
L73:   * PGWP eligible and
L74:   * at least 8 months (or 900 hours for Quebec credentials) in length
L75: You can’t get a PGWP if you already had one after completing an earlier program of study.
L76: ## If your passport expires before your PGWP
L77: 
L78: Make sure your passport is 【12†valid】 for the full length of time you’re eligible for a PGWP before you apply.
L79: 
L80: Your work permit will only be issued for the period your passport is valid. If your passport expires before the full duration of your eligibility, you can apply to extend your PGWP.
L81: 
L82: To extend your PGWP, you must 【8†apply on paper】 after you get a new passport that’s valid for the entire period you’re eligible for the work permit.

L37: # How your family members can come to Canada
L38: 
L39: Your family members can’t come with you to Canada under the IEC program. However, they can apply to work, visit or study in Canada on their own. We’ll look at each application separately.
L40: 
L41: ## Work in Canada
L42: 
L43: If your family member wants to work in Canada, they have the following 2 options:
L44: ### Option 1: Apply separately for IEC
L45: 
L46: Your family member can submit their own profile to the IEC program. They must meet the requirements and follow the application steps if they’re 【14†invited to apply for a work permit】.
L47: 
L48: 【9†Create an IEC profile】
L49: ### Option 2: Apply for a work permit outside of IEC
L50: 
L51: Family members of some foreign workers may be able to apply for an open work permit. An open work permit lets you work for most employers in Canada. Your family member can only apply for an open work permit after you’re approved as an IEC participant. Make sure they’re eligible before they submit an application.
L52: 
L53: 【15†Learn more about open work permits】
L54: In other cases, your family member may need to apply for an employer-specific work permit. An employer-specific work permit allows an employer to hire someone for a specific job.
L55: 
L56: 【16†Learn more about employer-specific work permits】
L57: ### Minimum age to work
L58: 
L59: Before your 【17†dependent children】 work in Canada, check the minimum age required to work in the province or territory and in the job type they plan to work in. Canadian employers must follow provincial labour laws.
L60: 
L61: Open work permit holders must also meet federal, provincial or territorial labour laws.
L62: 
L63: ## Visit or study in Canada
L64: 
L65: Your family member may choose to apply to come to Canada to visit or study.
L66: ### Visit Canada
L67: 
L68: Most people need a visitor visa or an electronic travel authorization (eTA) to travel to Canada. What you need depends on your 【18†passport or travel document】 and how you plan to enter Canada.
L69: 
L70: Most visitors can stay for up to 6 months in Canada.
L71: 
L72: 【19†Find out if you need a visa or an eTA†ircc.canada.ca】
L73: ### Study in Canada
L74: 
L75: The study permit is a document we issue that lets you study at a 【20†designated learning institution】 in Canada. Most people need a study permit to study in Canada for longer than 6 months.
L76: 
L77: 【21†Find out if you need a study permit】

L37: # Create your IEC profile and get your invitation to apply
L38: 
L39: To participate in IEC, your first step is to create and submit your profile in one or more IEC pools. After you submit your profile, you must wait for an Invitation to Apply (ITA) to apply for a work permit.
L40: 
L41: We regularly invite eligible applicants from IEC pools to apply for a work permit.
L42: 
L43:  If you want to start working in Canada in the next 12 months, you should create and submit your profile as soon as possible.
L44: ## 2026 IEC season is closed
L45: 
L46: The pools for the 2026 season are closed.
L47: 
L48: 【8†Check the rounds of invitations†ircc.canada.ca】 for key dates and available spots.
L49: ## On this page

L57: Tip: You may want to open this page in a different browser, tab or window while you complete your profile. You can then refer back to this information as needed.
L58: ## Step 1: Use the IRCC secure account to check your eligibility
L59: 
L60: Create or sign in to your account and select “International Experience Canada” to start the questionnaire and check your eligibility. Your answers will be saved automatically to help complete your profile.
L61: 
L62: The questionnaire takes 10 minutes to complete. You’ll be asked about your
L63:   * country of citizenship
L64:   * country of permanent residence (where you live permanently)
L65:     * This is the country where you have a permanent address. For example, if you’re a Mexican student in Canada, your country of permanent residence is Mexico.
L66:   * country of residence (where you live now)
L67:   * student status (if this applies to you)
L68:   * job offer (if this applies to you)
L69:   * confirmation letter from an IEC 【19†recognized organization】 (if this applies to you)
L70:     * Recognized organizations are different from 【20†representatives】, who can help with your immigration or citizenship application.
L71: 【4†Create or sign in to your IRCC secure account】
L72: ## Step 2: Complete your IEC profile
L73: 
L74: When you’re done with the questionnaire (and if you’re eligible), you can complete and submit your IEC profile online.
L75: 
L76: We use your answers to start your profile. To complete your profile, you need your passport. You also need to tell us about your:
L77: 
L78:   * identity (full names, date of birth, place of birth etc.)
L79:   * contact information
L80: 
L81: If you’re invited to apply, you’ll use your IRCC secure account to:
L82:   * submit your work permit application
L83:   * pay your fees
L84:   * check the status of your application
L85: 
L86: You must use your IRCC secure account to apply for an IEC work permit.
L87: ### When you fill out the online forms
L88: 
L89:   * Leave out any commas that separate your first or last names (if you have more than one first or last name). For example, use “Julie Louise Marie” if your first name is “Julie, Louise, Marie”.
L90:   * Use English and French letters only.
L91:   * If your passport uses other special letters or characters, use the letter without the accent. For example, use “z” instead of “ź.”

L130:

L191: If you submitted your study permit application on or after November 1, 2024, you must graduate in an 【15†eligible field of study】.
L192: 
L193: If you submitted your study permit application before November 1, 2024
L194: 
L195: You don’t need to meet the field of study requirements.
L196: 
L197: If you graduated from any other college, polytechnic or non-university program
L198: #### Language requirement:
L199: 
L200: You must 【21†prove your English or French language skills】 with a minimum level of Canadian Language Benchmarks (CLB) 5 in English or Niveaux de competence linguistique canadiens (NCLC) 5 in French in all 4 language areas.
L201: 
L202: 【7†Find out what your language level is based on your language test results】.
L203: 
L204: If you submitted your PGWP application before November 1, 2024
L205: 
L206: You don’t need to meet the language requirement for your program.
L207: #### Field of study requirement:
L208: 
L209: If you submitted your study permit application on or after November 1, 2024, you must have graduated in an 【15†eligible field of study】.
L210: 
L211: If you submitted your study permit application before November 1, 2024
L212: 
L213: You don’t need to meet the field of study requirements.
L214: 
L215: If you graduated from a flight school
L216: 
L217: If you graduated from a flight school, you must also meet one of the following requirements:
L218:   * You completed a flight training course at a DLI training centre and now have a Canadian commercial pilot’s license or
L219:   * You have or are getting an instructor’s rating and have a job offer as a flight instructor from a DLI flight training centre
L220: 
L221: There are no language or field of study requirements for graduates from a PGWP-eligible flight school.
L222: ## Eligibility requirements based on your physical location
L223: 
L224: There are different eligibility requirements depending on if you’re a graduate applying for a PGWP from within or outside of Canada.
L225: 
L226: In Canada graduates
L227: 
L228: You’re eligible to apply if you meet all other eligibility requirements and are a graduate living in Canada.
L229: 
L230: Don’t let your status expire while you wait for your marks.
L231: 
L232: If your study permit will expire before you get your marks, you have 2 options. You can either
L233:   * 【22†apply for a visitor record】 to stay in Canada longer or
L234:   * leave Canada and apply for your PGWP
L235: 
L236: If you stay in Canada and let your permit expire, you must apply to 【23†restore your status】 as a student to apply for your PGWP. To restore your status, you must pay additional fees.
L237: 
L238: Outside Canada graduates
L239: 
L240: You may be eligible to apply for a PGWP as a graduate outside of Canada if you meet the eligibility requirements for 【19†distance learning】.
L241: If you completed your study program in Canada, you may also leave and then apply for your PGWP from outside Canada.
L242: ## Field of study requirements
L243: 
L244: If your 【13†study program】 has a field of study requirement, you must graduate from a program linked to certain occupations in long-term shortage.
L245: 
L246: 【8†Learn which fields of study are eligible for PGWP field of study requirements】.

L248: ### Other types of work permits
L249: 
L250: If you’re not eligible for a PGWP, you may still be able to work in Canada after you graduate.

L44: #### 3. We process your application
L45: 
L46: After we get your biometrics, we start processing your application. See 【11†how long it takes to process your application.】
L47: 
L48: If we need more information from you, we’ll contact you.
L49: 
L50: #### 4. We make a decision on your application
L51: 
L52: When we finish reviewing your application, we let you know if you’re approved to come to Canada. If you are, we issue your documents.
L53: 
L55: #### 5. You travel to Canada (if you’re approved)
L56: 
L57: Make sure you travel with the documents we gave you. This includes travel documents like a visitor visa, study or work permits or an eTA (electronically linked to your passport).
L58: 
L59: Airline staff and border service officers at ports of entry will ask to see your travel documents. If you don’t have them, you may not be able to board your flight to Canada.
L60: 
L61: Make sure children under 18 travel with the 【12†right documents】.
L62: #### 6. We check your identity when you arrive in Canada
L63: 
L64: When you arrive, we check your identity to make sure that you are the same person who was approved to travel to Canada. We may use your biometrics to do this.
L65: 
L66: If we can’t verify your identity, you may be detained by a border services officer. These officers help protect the health and safety of Canadians.
L67: If the officer determines that you’re not admissible to Canada, you won’t be allowed to enter Canada. If you came by air, you’ll have to take a return flight to where you came from.
L68: #### 7. You’re allowed to enter Canada
L69: 
L70: If you pass the identity check and meet the 【13†entry requirements】, the border services officer stamps your passport and lets you know how long you can stay in Canada. You’re normally allowed to stay in Canada for up to six months.
L71: 
L72: Children under 18 must meet the same entry requirements as adults. The border services officer may ask minor children to show 【12†other documents】 depending on whether the child is travelling alone or with someone.
L73: ### Basic entry requirements
L74: 
L75: You must meet some basic requirements to enter Canada. You must:
L76:   * have a valid travel document, like a passport
L77:   * be in good health
L78:   * have no criminal or immigration-related convictions
L79:   * convince an immigration officer that you have ties—such as a job, home, financial assets or family—that will take you back to your home country
L80:   * convince an immigration officer that you will leave Canada at the end of your visit
L81:   * have enough money for your stay
L82:     * The amount of money you will need depends on how long you will stay and if you will stay in a hotel, or with friends or relatives.
L83: Some people are not admissible to Canada, which means they are not allowed to enter the country. You can be inadmissible for several reasons, including being involved in:
L84: 
L85:   * criminal activity
L86:   * human rights violations
L87:   * organized crime
L88: 
L89: You can also be inadmissible for security, health or financial reasons.
L90: 
L91: 【14†Find out more about inadmissibility】.

L95:   * Families applying at the same time: maximum total fee of CAD $170
