L106: # How to apply
L107: 
L108: You can apply for a post-graduation work permit (PGWP) from within Canada or from another country, as long as you’re eligible.
L109: 
L110: You have up to 180 days after you graduate to apply for a PGWP.
L111: 
L112: If your study permit expires before you apply
L113: 
L114: If you don’t change your status to visitor and your study permit expires, you have up to 90 days after your study permit expires to apply for a PGWP and restore your status as a student.
L115: 
L116: To restore your status as a student, you must
L117:   * apply online for your PGWP and pay the correct fee ($255), and
L118:   * pay the fee to restore your status as a student (Error loading fee. 【21†Check the fee list†ircc.canada.ca】.)
L119:     * Because of system limitations, you must 【22†pay the fees to restore your status as a student online†eservices.cic.gc.ca】 and attach a copy of the receipt to your PGWP online application. You don’t need to make a separate application to restore your status as a student.
L120: You can’t work until your work permit has been approved. 【23†Find out if you meet the other requirements to work while we process your application】.
L121: 
L122: If you don’t apply within 90 days, or if 90 days have already passed, you must leave Canada.
L123: 
L124: Your study permit must be valid (not expired) at the time you submit your application to be eligible to work in Canada while awaiting a decision on your PGWP application.
L125: 
L126: If you need to extend or change the conditions of your PGWP
L127: You must 【24†apply on paper】 if you’re extending or changing the conditions of your PGWP.
L128: 
L129: You can only extend your PGWP if your passport expired earlier than the full period of eligibility of your PGWP. If your passport expired earlier than the length of time you’re eligible, we will only issue you a PGWP that’s valid until your passport expires.
L130: 
L131: This should be written in a note on your initial PGWP.
L132: You may need to change the conditions on your PGWP if you need to provide an additional document, like a medical exam, after you already applied.
L133: 
L134: You don’t have to provide proof of language ability if you apply to extend your PGWP because your passport expired before the end of the full validity period of the PGWP you’re eligible for.
L135: 
L136: How to remove the job restrictions on your PGWP
L137: There may be restrictions on your PGWP because you didn’t have a 【25†medical exam】 before you came to Canada. These restrictions prevent you from working in
L138:   * jobs that bring you into close contact with people, such as
L139:     * workers in health care settings
L140:     * clinical laboratory workers
L141:     * patient attendants in nursing and geriatric homes
L142:     * medical students admitted to Canada to attend university
L143:     * medical electives and physicians on short-term locums
L144:     * workers in primary or secondary school settings or workers in child care settings
L145:     * domestics
L146:     * workers who give in-home care to children, the elderly or people with disabilities
L147:     * day nursery employees
L148:     * other similar jobs
L149:   * jobs in agriculture if you’ve visited or lived in 1 of 【26†these countries】 for more than 6 months during the past year
L150: You must get a medical exam within 90 days of your arrival. You will need a chest X-ray and blood test.
L151: 
L152: You may need to pay a fee for this exam.
L153: 
L154: Once you get your medical exam results, you can ask to have these restrictions removed. To do this, you must 【24†apply on paper to change the conditions on your PGWP】.
L155: ## Apply online
L156: 
L157: In most cases, you must apply online for a PGWP.
L158: 
L159: ### Step 1: Make sure you have what you need
L160: 
L161: To apply online, you’ll need
L162: 
L163:   * a scanner or camera to create electronic copies of your documents
L164:   * a valid 【27†credit】 or 【28†debit】 card
L165: ## Credit cards and prepaid cards
L166: 
L167: We accept credit cards and prepaid cards from:
L168: 
L169:     * Visa^{®},
L170:     * MasterCard^{®},
L171:     * American Express^{®}, and
L172:     * JCB.
L173: 
L174: If you use a prepaid credit card, keep it for at least 18 months after you pay to make refunds easier.
L175: 
L176: We also accept all Visa Debit cards.
L177: 
L178: The card you use does not have to be in your name. The cardholder’s name will appear on the receipt but it does not need to match your application.
L179: ## Debit cards
L180: 
L181: It must:
L182: 
L183:     * be from a Canadian bank using 【29†INTERAC^{®} Online†www.interac.ca】, and
L184:     * be registered for online banking through your bank’s website.
L185: 
L186: We also accept all Visa Debit cards. If your card has the Visa Debit logo on it, alone or with the INTERAC^{®} Online logo, select Visa Debit as your payment method.
L187: 
L188: The card you use does not have to be in your name. The cardholder’s name will appear on the receipt but it does not need to match your application.
L189: ### Step 2: Read the instruction guide
L190: 
L191: You should read the applicable guide for your situation before you complete your application. The guide will explain how to complete each field on the form.
L192: 
L193: If you’re applying online from outside Canada, 【30†read guide 5487 – applying for a work permit outside Canada】.
L194: 
L195: If you’re applying online from inside Canada, 【31†read guide 5580 – Applying for a work permit – online application】.
L196: ### Step 3: Prepare your answers for the online tool
L197: 
L198: Before you can upload your forms, you must answer some questions in your IRCC secure account.
L199: 
L200: Use the “I do not have a Personal Reference Code” option and choose the “Visitor visa, study and/or work permit” button to answer the questionnaire in your account. We use your answers to create a personalized document checklist for you.
L201: When you fill out the PDF forms, your answers must be accurate. If you’re currently residing in Canada, use your Canadian address regardless of which instructions you’re using to apply.
L202: 
L203: Special instructions to submit proof of language results or eligible field of study
L204: After you’ve logged into your account and completed the questionnaire, your PGWP document checklist will list the proof of language results as an optional document. You must include this proof with your application if it’s a requirement for your 【32†study program】.
L205: Due to system limitations, the document checklist won’t ask you to provide proof that you graduated from an eligible field of study. If you’re required to provide proof that you graduated from an eligible field of study, you must upload it in the “Client information” section of your account.
L206: 
L207: 【19†How to submit proof that you graduated from an eligible field of study】
L208: ### Step 4: Know the fees you have to pay
L209: 
L210: In most cases, your fees will include processing fees for you and anyone you include on your application.
L211: 
L212: We’ll ask you to pay your fees at the end of your application. Make sure you pay both the open work permit holder fee and the work permit fee.
L213: #### Third-party fees
L214: 
L215: Depending on your situation, you may need to pay third parties for:
L216: 
L217:   * 【33†medical exams】
L218:   * 【34†police certificates】
L219:   * language tests
L220:   * services at a Visa Application Centre, if you use one.
L221: 
L222: If you need to use any of these services, you’ll pay these fees directly to the third party.
L223: #### Biometrics fee
L224: 
L225: In most cases, you should pay a biometrics fee when you submit your application. Otherwise you may experience delays. The biometrics fee covers the cost of collecting fingerprints and a digital photo. 【35†Find out if you need to give your biometrics】.

L293: ## Eligibility by countries or territories and categories
L294: ### Andorra—Working Holiday
L295: 
L296: Description: The Working Holiday category is designed for Andorran citizens who intend to travel in Canada and who wish to find temporary paid employment to help pay for their trip (up to 12 months).
L297: 
L298: Note: As an Andorran citizen, you may 【6†participate】 in IEC only once.
L299: 
L300: To be eligible for the Working Holiday category, you must:
L301:   * be an Andorran citizen
L302:   * have a 【7†valid】 Andorran 【7†passport】 for the duration of your stay in Canada
L303:     * Your work permit in Canada can’t be valid longer than your passport
L304:   * be between the ages of 18 and 30 (inclusive)
L305:   * have a minimum of CAN$2,500 to help cover your expenses in Canada
L306:   * have 【8†health insurance】 for the duration of your stay
L307:     * You may have to present evidence of this insurance when you enter Canada
L308:   * not be 【9†inadmissible】 to Canada
L309:   * have, before departure, a round-trip ticket or demonstrate that you’ll have the financial resources to purchase a departure ticket at the end of your authorized stay in Canada
L310:   * 【10†not be accompanied by dependants】
L311:   * 【11†pay the fees】
